label: vision_footnote
text: Bittles of Lexington, and Concord, the first of the Revolutionary War, which took place April 18, 1775, were re-enacted, at the one hundred and fiftieth anniversary of these historic conflicts on the same spots when modern Minute Men, garbed in Revolutionary uniforms, battled the red coats. This photo was taken at the Concord bridge. Preceding the battle, there was a parade of the modern Minute Men in Concord.

label: vision_footnote
text: Prince Henry, has had the title of Duke of Edinburgh "conferred" upon him by the reports from England, being hailed all over as "Duke of Edinburgh."

label: vision_footnote
text: The United States Navy Department at Washington is giving serious consideration to the proposed naval base for government ships at Alameda, near Oakland, Mr. Curtis D. Wilbur, Secretary of the Navy, is shown studying a map of the plot, embracing five thousand acres.

label: vision_footnote
text: MR. C. C. Faiman, of Chicago, wife of the bacteriologist, whose confession resulted in indictment of himself and William D. Shepherd for the "murder by inoculation with typhoid germs" of Billy McClintock.

label: vision_footnote
text: Jack O'Dean, proprietor of an inn, was blown to bits when he stopped on the self starter of his motor car, thereby setting off a picnic acid bomb, which had been placed beneath the floor of the car. The victim's wife was a witness to the explosion, which hurled O'Dean more than twenty-five feet, completely demolished the car, and smashed windows in nearby houses. It is believed that the informal machine was placed in the car by enemy gangsters.

text: Mr. and Mrs. Henry Ford were among the guests at the wedding of Theodore Miller Edison, son of the famous inventor, and Miss Anna Marie Ostorhout, daughter of a Harvard professor, at Cambridge, Mass. Shown, left to right, are: Bishop Anderson, who performed the ceremony; Mrs. Ford, Harvey Firestone, the manufacturer, and Ford.

text: Perhaps one of the strangest weddings ever witnessed took place when Miss Gabrielle Gunther, formerly a resident of Germany and known throughout the world's circus side shows as the "half woman," because she was born legless, was married to Johnde Fuller, a business man of normal physique.
